text:
Today, tax automation has a **shared core under `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations`**, with provider namespaces supplying vendor behavior. **Instead is the only registered adapter.** `FirmSettings` already lists `juno`, `gruntworx`, and `instead`, but enum membership alone does not make a provider operational; Juno remains outside these ports. See [Registry](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:3).

The vendor-neutral ports are ordinary service classes, backed by shared models and concerns:

| Area | Existing ports and responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Authorization and connections | `Authorizations::Create`; `Connections::{Create, Find, Disconnect, DisconnectAll, Renew, Revoke}` and async wrappers. Own policy checks, provider selection, switching, account binding, and grant lifecycle. |
| Export | `ExportAsync` and `Export::ValidateDocuments`. Validate the request and each file, create shared records, then delegate the actual send. Return accepted and rejected documents in one response. |
| Document lifecycle | `Documents::{UpdateStatus, BroadcastStatus, FailUpload, ResumeSends}` and helpers. Own normalized statuses, failure reasons, notifications, and reconnect recovery. |
| Shared upload utility | `Documents::TransferBytesToPresignedTarget`, backed by `UploadTargetBuffer`. Available for adapters using signed upload targets. |
| Preparation and lifecycle cleanup | `TaxPreparations::{FindOrCreate, BatchDestroy, DestroyForClient, DestroyForContact, MergeForContact}`, firm cleanup, and `TaxPreparationPrefills::Find`. |

For example, the [export port](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export_async.rb:53) resolves the connection and passport, validates files, creates shared send records, and hands those records to the adapter. Provider webhooks and reconciliation translate vendor statuses into the shared [status-update port](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/update_status.rb:33).

**Adapter registration is explicit.** `Registry::ADAPTERS` maps a provider symbol to its namespace; `FEATURE_FLAGS` optionally controls availability. Lookup normally follows the firm’s settings, while historical work can resolve an adapter directly from a send record’s saved provider. Unknown providers raise `UnknownProviderError`.

The namespace must supply the constants and methods the core calls:

| Adapter member | Expected contract |
|---|---|
| `Connection` | `.for_firm(firm)`, `.usable_for(firm)`, `.capabilities`, and the shared connection lifecycle/token interface. Instead includes `HasOauthConnection` and `HasCapabilities`. |
| `Client` | Constructible with a connection; supports token renewal/revocation and applicable transport operations. Instead subclasses `BaseClient`, which includes `TokenRefreshable`. |
| `Authorizations::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, return_url)` |
| `Connections::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, params)` |
| `ExportAsync` | `.call(user, actor, tax_preparation, tax_automation_documents: records)` |
| `DestroyForTaxPreparations` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, tax_preparations)` |
| `DestroyForFirm` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id)` |
| `MergeForContact` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, source_contact_id, target_contact_id)` |

These services use the existing `ServiceResult` convention. This is a convention enforced by callers, rather than a formal adapter interface checked at registration. The registry does not prescribe the provider’s upload workflow: Instead implements entity lookup/creation followed by start-upload → byte transfer → finalize-upload in its own [workflow](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/workers/tax_preparation/tax_automations/instead/documents/export_async_workflow.rb:24).

The current reusable connection infrastructure is specifically OAuth-oriented. [HasOauthConnection](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/concerns/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_oauth_connection.rb:23) provides encrypted credentials and `disconnected / connected / expired / revoked` states. An expired connection remains usable while refresh can recover it. `BaseClient` supplies shared transport, error handling, and OAuth mechanics; adapters declare OAuth settings and implement vendor hooks.

**The capability passport is a typed, computed description of a vendor.** It lives on `Connection.capabilities`, so reading it requires no connection record. [HasCapabilities](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_capabilities.rb:21) builds a `Dry::Struct` containing:

```text
Capabilities
  terms[]
    return_type
    accepted_file_formats[]
    max_file_size_mb
  supported_tax_years[]
```

An adapter implements private class methods `capability_terms` and `supported_tax_years`. Terms can be declared for groups of return types; the concern expands them and rejects duplicate declarations. Formats must be canonical lowercase extensions, sizes positive integers, and years between 2000 and the current year plus one. Missing implementations and malformed declarations fail when `.capabilities` is called.

Export validation uses this passport for unsupported return types, years, formats, and file sizes. The [API serializer](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/serializers/tax_preparation/base/tax_automations/connection_serializer.rb:60) exposes `tax_years` and enriched `return_types`, each with `value`, `name`, personal/business `type`, `file_types`, and `file_size_limit`.

Instead currently declares all 11 mapped IRS return types, the current year and two preceding years, and configurable file terms. Defaults are PDF, CSV, DOCX, ODS, ODT, PPTX, TXT, XLSX, and a size limit of 2000 MB.

**The data model separates shared sending state from vendor handles:**

| Model | Role and key relationships |
|---|---|
| [FirmSettings](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/firm_settings.rb:6) | One row per firm. Stores the selected provider and persistent `external_tenant_uuid` account binding. |
| [TaxPreparation](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparation.rb:3) | Shared preparation envelope, still stored in `juno_tax_preparations`. Core identity is `(firm, client, contact, year)`; carries return type, EIN, and business name. Business returns can have no contact. Legacy Juno relationships remain. |
| [Document](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:3) | Shared send record linking a source TaxDome document to a preparation. Unique by `(firm, preparation, document, provider, return_type)`. Provider and return type are snapshots. Owns upload/processing state, failure reason, and upload timestamp. |
| `Instead::Connection` | One grant per firm, its staff creator, encrypted credentials, and Instead-specific PKCE ceremony fields. |
| `Instead::Entity` | Vendor taxpayer identity: external UUID, entity type, optional client/contact linkage, source, names, and sync/archive metadata. Survives across preparation years. |
| `Instead::Document` | One-to-one extension of a shared send record. Holds the Instead entity, external file UUID, and vendor path. |

Shared upload states are `waiting / uploading / uploaded / failed`; processing states are `sent / processing / processed / error / archived / exceeded`. Vendor-specific statuses must be mapped into these.

Provider switching is completed transactionally in [Connections::Create](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/connections/create.rb:42): it selects the new provider, opens and binds its connection, disconnects the displaced connection, and schedules recovery. Historical sends retain their original provider.

For GruntWorx, the existing extension point is therefore a registered namespace implementing these contracts, with its own workflow and vendor data tables. Its enum value is already reserved; its adapter is not implemented in the current registry. No files were changed.
